text: Mesophilic lactococci sour boiled milk into a soft set curd; diacetyl-forming Lc. diacetylactis and Leuconostoc give mild dahi its buttery note, while added thermophiles make a sourer dahi. Household dahi is backslopped from the previous batch, so its flora varies, with Lactobacillus and Streptococcus often dominant. The 37 °C, 5–8 h route with added thermophiles gives a sourer, yoghurt-like dahi.
